Olivia B.: Hi team, I was just granted temporary guardianship for my niece (age 6) due to foster placement. Can I add her to medical midyear? What paperwork do you need?

Asha (People Ops): Hi Olivia  sorry for the situation. Short answer: yes, foster placement/guardianship is generally a QLE. We need official placement or court docs. Which type of paperwork do you have right now?

Olivia B.: I have the county child placement letter (dated 2026-02-10), a temporary guardianship order from juvenile court (signed 2026-02-08), and school registration showing her address with me.

Asha (People Ops): That's a good bundle. Typical required docs for foster/temporary guardianship additions:``
- Court order for temporary guardianship or foster care placement letter
- Placement agency letter showing effective placement date and caseworker contact
- Proof of residency (school enrollment or lease)
- Government ID for the child (birth certificate or passport)``
Also, carriers usually want documents uploaded within 30 days of the QLE date (placement or court order date).

Max (Benefits Ops): Adding: Once you upload, we'll submit to the carrier as a QLE (event date = 2026-02-08 / court order). Carriers vary on effective date: many permit coverage effective on the placement/court date; some use first of next month. If approved retroactive, we'll adjust payroll and backdate premiums accordingly.

Olivia B.: Great. Where do I upload? Any redaction rules?

Asha (People Ops): Upload via the secure benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/upload choose "Dependent QLE - Foster/Guardianship". Redact full SSNs; last four digits okay. If any docs are in the county portal screenshot format, include the caseworker contact info too.

Olivia B.: Uploaded files: "olivia_foster_bundle_1845001245.pdf" (court order + placement letter + school record).

Benefits Bot: Upload received from Olivia B.  File ID: up_1845001246  Status: awaiting manual review.

Max (Benefits Ops): I'll review now. Quick check list for carriers: temporary guardianship + placement letter + proof child lives with you = strong case. If carrier requests more, they often want a caseworker contact or a sworn affidavit confirming placement date. I'll flag the caseworker in the submission to speed verification.

Legal Ops Bot: Reminder: do not post PHI in channel. Use secure upload only. Redact full SSNs and bank details.

Lina (Payroll): FYI payroll will need the carrier's effective date to calculate deductions. If carrier approves retro to 02/08/2026, we'll do a one-time payroll catch-up in the next cycle. If effective is future, deductions start on the first payroll after that date. Expect 1 payroll cycle for the change to reflect.

Olivia B.: Thanks  anything I should expect if carrier denies retroactive coverage?

Max (Benefits Ops): If carrier denies retroactive effective date, they'll typically allow enrollment effective the carrier-specified date (often next month). We can appeal with placement caseworker notes if needed, but appeals take longer. We'll keep you posted.

Asha (People Ops): I'll review once Max flags anything missing. Olivia, DM me if you want an estimate of payroll adjustment once we have the effective date.

Max (Benefits Ops): Document review started at 1845001258. Preliminary: documents look complete. Submitting to carrier now; SLA ~5-10 business days. Case# C-184500.

Benefits Bot: Carrier submission completed for C-184500. Expected carrier decision window: 7 business days.

Olivia B.: Thank you everyone  I really appreciate the help and quick replies.

Max (Benefits Ops): Will update here when carrier responds. If carrier approves retro, Lina will calculate the payroll adjustment and we'll notify you via DM.

Lina (Payroll): Copy  I'll standby and prepare an estimate when Max posts the effective date.

Asha (People Ops): Thanks team. Olivia, sending a DM with next steps and the affidavit template in case carrier asks for it later. :heart:
